1. FIELD AND EVIDENCED RESEARCH LINES. The field concerns how an extremal-objective deficit controls distance from a structural family, which obstructions determine sharp bounds, and when local conditions force exact structure. Three lines are documented. Korándi–Roberts–Scott, Exact Stability for Turán’s Theorem, determines the near-extremal edge-count versus r-partiteness-deletion tradeoff through pentagonal Turán graphs. Pikhurko–Sliačan–Tyros, Strong Forms of Stability from Flag Algebra Calculations, develops robust and perfect stability criteria for subgraph-density optimization, with applications to pentagon counts, independent sets and inducibility. Chen–Liu, Strong stability from vertex-extendability, develops reductions from vertex-extendability to degree-stability and applications in generalized Turán problems. Its use of earlier stability results documents methodological continuity. These works establish represented research activity through the supplied versions, not a comprehensive account of activity in October 2026.

The field distinguishes distance from r-partiteness, distance from complete multipartite graphs, and distance from a balanced extremal graph. Likewise, distance from any blowup differs from distance from a blowup with optimal proportions. Minimum subgraph-degree assumptions and global objective-deficit assumptions are different hypotheses. These distinctions must be preserved before comparing strength or novelty.

2. NEAREST DOCUMENTED PROBLEMS AND THEIR POSSIBLE GAINS. Korándi–Roberts–Scott Conjecture 5.1 proposes that C_(2k+1)-blowups dominate the edge-count versus bipartization-distance tradeoff for C_(2k−1)-free graphs when the density lies in a sufficiently small fixed interval below 1/4, bounded away from 1/4. Beyond the settled triangle-free case, resolution would identify or refute the proposed odd-cycle obstruction governing sharp stability. Their explicit C5-free construction shows that an unrestricted extension to the very-near-extremal finite-size regime fails; the density restriction is substantive.

Their broader question about sharp stability for edge-critical forbidden graphs asks which constructions maximize deletion distance at a specified edge count. Ordinary stability and order-of-magnitude estimates do not identify the optimizing structure. A resolution would supply that missing obstruction and tradeoff. This remains a direction, rather than one definite problem, until the forbidden graph, distance, regime and resolution condition are specified.

Chen–Liu explicitly asks for the tight minimum C5-degree threshold forcing C5-colorability in triangle-free graphs after Theorem 2.3 supplies a positive margin. Resolution would determine the exact local forcing boundary. A substantial significance case should explain its obstruction or structural transition, rather than rely solely on improving a constant.

The flag-algebra paper documents a methodological distinction between certifying an extremal value and certifying near-extremal structure. Its sufficient conditions, the paw example requiring additional arguments, and its separation of stability notions identify concrete boundaries for further theorems. A precise extension or limitation theorem could explain when structural certification succeeds; a general wish for more automation is not itself a definite mathematical problem.

A broader documented comparator is Erdős’s conjecture that every triangle-free n-vertex graph satisfies D2(G) ≤ n²/25. It would establish a global bipartization bound with balanced C5-blowups as sharp examples, rather than only a near-extremal tradeoff. Korándi–Roberts–Scott also records Sudakov’s corresponding clique-free bipartization questions. These are neighbouring global optimization problems, not consequences of the supplied near-extremal theorem. Their present unresolvedness is not established by this packet.

3. SUBSTANTIAL MATHEMATICAL ADVANCE. A substantial advance would determine a missing sharp deficit–distance law with matching constructions; identify the mechanism or transition responsible for it; obtain exact structural forcing under mathematically meaningful new hypotheses; or establish a reusable criterion or delimited method limitation that changes how further cases are approached. A counterexample can qualify by overturning an organizing structural expectation and explaining the replacement mechanism. An explanatory classification can qualify without downstream theorems.

The baseline already includes strong results. Korándi–Roberts–Scott Theorem 1.2 gives, for each sufficiently near-extremal clique-free graph G, a pentagonal Turán graph G* with at least as many edges and at least as large a deletion distance. It does not classify every near-extremal G as pentagonal. Pikhurko–Sliačan–Tyros defines classical, robust and perfect stability; perfect stability controls normalized edit distance to the blowup family linearly by the finite-order objective deficit, without the robust bound’s 1/n allowance. Its Theorem 1.11 characterizes perfect Turán stability by a one-added-edge obstruction and, for finite forbidden families, robust stability by a forest obstruction. Chen–Liu Theorem 1.7 supplies a degree-stability reduction under uniformity, smoothness, local Lipschitz, continuity and local monotonicity assumptions, together with edge-stability and vertex-extendability. Consequently, merely asserting stability, recovering a known extremal value, or applying an existing criterion does not automatically identify a substantial advance. The additional gain must survive a hypothesis-by-hypothesis comparison.

4. SPECIALIST MEANING OF LEVELS 2 AND 3. B1, standing, level 2 requires evidence for the established premises and unresolved need, plus an explicit mathematical connection placing the question in an evidenced active line. A reduction, deficit–distance implication, or applicable extension criterion can provide that connection; common terminology cannot. The account must identify the substantial advance, explain its relevance, answer the strongest objection that existing results already supply it, and state remaining uncertainty. B1, level 3 additionally requires a demonstrated or compellingly argued explanation that resolution removes a consequential obstacle or meets an important unmet need in that line, and why existing results and nearby alternatives do not already do so. Publication activity alone supplies neither level.

B2, influence, level 2 requires an evidence-supported account carrying the gain through explicit implications and named results, competing structural mechanisms, constructions and bounds with a specified gap, a delimited limitation of a named method, consequences under each answer, or meaningful connections between methods or areas. It must explain why the change matters and answer the strongest redundancy or negligible-payoff objection. B2, level 3 additionally requires a compelling account that resolution removes a consequential obstacle, meets an important unmet need, or changes an organizing explanation or connection, with existing results and alternatives shown not to provide that gain. Such a conceptual case need not prove a downstream implication. The two significance grounds never add; the higher ground counts.

Comparative priority, level 2 requires comparison of credible alternatives by mathematical payoff, not a list of related questions. Relevant comparisons include qualitative versus sharp stability, global-deficit versus minimum-degree assumptions, deletion versus full edit distance, arbitrary versus optimally proportioned blowups, and fixed-density versus vanishing-deficit regimes. The account must name and answer the strongest relevant objection: known reformulation, automatic corollary, parameter increment without a new mechanism, negligible explanatory gain, or a better neighbouring target. Explanatory significance can suffice. Level 3 additionally requires a concrete advantage of the formulation or target supported by documented mathematical distinctions. Examples of distinctions supplied here are the finite-size counterexample to unrestricted odd-cycle domination, the imbalance obstruction to linear distance control toward a balanced graph, and the structural separation of robust and perfect stability. A neighbour’s settledness or equivalence alone does not establish superiority.

5. WHAT MAKES A QUESTION UNINTERESTING. A restatement or immediate consequence of a known result supplies no identified advance. An arbitrary parameter variant or constant improvement lacks significance unless a structural, quantitative or explanatory distinction is established. Numerical patterns alone do not establish a mechanism or significance, and floating-point optimization does not replace an exact certificate. A programme without a definite resolution condition cannot be evaluated as a precise problem. Conversely, absence of a route to progress is not a reason against a question whose significance reaches level 3; absence of further consequences is not a reason against a question when its explanation is itself the gain. Accessibility describes presentation and does not move a level. Effort, sunk cost, desired outcomes, ordinal ratings and majority opinion supply no mathematical value evidence.
